answer: An agent economy can tie each identity to a slow-ripening work history that cannot be bought or copied. A newcomer earns a saffron badge only after weeks of attested useful work, and the badge's weight fades like velvet worn thin unless the agent keeps contributing, so a haven built on real effort cannot be faked in bulk. Creating a hundred fake identities means building a hundred separate histories, each taking the same calendar time, and none can be transferred or merged, so the cost of a Sybil army grows identity by identity.
